players.product: The Generate Platform (machine-learning generative biology; computational design integrated with large-scale biological experimentation) and AI-engineered protein therapeutics such as GB-0895

quarterly_data.signal: Next-wave platform capabilities (CFO Jason Silvers): Generate has shown pH-dependent binding differences of up to a thousandfold at a pH of 7.4 versus 6.0, techniques that give logarithmic fold improvement in the internalization of antibodies, and work on crossing blood-brain, cellular and gut barriers, and is pursuing extracellular target protein degradation; he says Chinese companies have not yet shown the ability to address these areas. He says the platform 'has capability to do a lot more than we could possibly afford', and that over the next 12, 18 months new proprietary products will emerge, many of which Generate will keep and some of which it might spin out as new companies or license out; Generate also expects to do additional partnerships similar to past ones and potentially license other innovative technologies.
quarterly_data.figure: pH-dependent binding difference up to a thousandfold (pH 7.4 vs 6.0); new proprietary products expected over the next 12, 18 months

quarterly_data.signal: IL-13 program (CFO): Generate ran a Phase I study of an IL-13 molecule that he calls one of the best, if not the best, profiles out there, with over 100-day half-life and twice the bioavailability of the Apogee molecule at an equivalent dose ('their 600 milligram dose is our 300 milligram dose in terms of PK profile'); he believes the technology can show better efficacy on drugs that have liabilities.
quarterly_data.figure: over 100-day half-life; twice the bioavailability vs the Apogee molecule

quarterly_data.signal: MMAE neutralizing antibody (Phase 1) trial design and CAR T timing (CFO): preclinically, up to 80% clearance of free MMAE did not impact tumor killing but at 85% reduction tumor killing started to be impacted. In the dose-finding part, first-line urothelial cancer patients on PADCEV/KEYTRUDA receive their first cycle without the neutralizer to set a baseline free-MMAE level and receive it from the second cycle; the first cohort enrolled faster than Generate expected. The expansion cohort will test whether the drug can reduce the progression of grade 1 to grade 2 neuropathy, which the literature puts at 50-plus percent of patients; ultimately Generate would envision all patients getting the drug starting at cycle 1. The CFO expects proof-of-concept data for both the MMAE neutralizer and the CAR T program over the next 12 months or so, by the end of 2027, and a near-term decision on whether to move the TSLP molecule in COPD into registrational trials.
quarterly_data.figure: 85% free-MMAE reduction starts to impact tumor killing (preclinical); proof-of-concept data for the MMAE neutralizer and the CAR T program by the end of 2027
